original_value: Vital sign monitoring is a common practice amongst medical professionals, and plays a key role in patient care and clinical diagnosis. Traditionally, dedicated equipment is employed to monitor these vital signs. For example, electrocardiograms (ECG) with 3-12 electrodes are attached to the target chest for heartbeat monitoring. In the last few years, wireless sensing becomes a hot research topic and wireless signal itself is utilized for sensing purposes without requiring the target to wear any sensors. The contact-free nature of wireless sensing makes it particularly appealing in current COVID-19 pandemic. Recently, promising progress has been achieved and the sensing granularity has been pushed to millimeter level, fine enough to monitor respiration which causes a chest displacement of 5 mm. While a great success with respiration monitoring, it is still very challenging to monitor heartbeat due to the extremely subtle chest displacement (0.1 - 0.5 mm) - smaller than 10% of that caused by respiration. What makes it worse is that the tiny heartbeat-caused chest displacement is buried inside the respiration-caused displacement. In this paper, we show the feasibility of employing the popular smart speakers (e.g., Amazon Echo) to monitor an individual's heartbeats in a contact-free manner. To extract the submillimeter heartbeat motion in the presence of other interference movements, a series of novel signal processing schemes are employed. We successfully prototype the first real-time heartbeat monitoring system using a commodity smart speaker. Experiment results show that the proposed system can monitor a target's heartbeat accurately, achieving a median heart rate estimation error of 0.75 beat per minute (bpm), and a median heartbeat interval estimation error of 13.28 ms (less than 1.8%), outperforming even some popular commodity products available on the market.

result.paraphrase: Vital sign monitoring is widely used by medical professionals and is essential for patient care and clinical diagnosis. In the past, it typically relied on dedicated equipment; for instance, electrocardiograms (ECG) use 3-12 electrodes attached to the chest to track heartbeats. In recent years, wireless sensing has emerged as a major research area, using wireless signals themselves for sensing without requiring a person to wear sensors. Its contact-free nature is especially attractive during the COVID-19 pandemic. Significant progress has recently pushed sensing granularity to the millimeter level, precise enough to monitor respiration, which causes about 5 mm of chest displacement. Although respiration monitoring has seen great success, heartbeat monitoring remains very difficult because the chest displacement it causes is extremely subtle, at 0.1 - 0.5 mm, less than 10% of the displacement caused by respiration. To make matters worse, this tiny heartbeat-induced motion is embedded within respiration-induced movement. In this paper, we demonstrate that popular smart speakers, such as Amazon Echo, can be used to monitor an individual's heartbeats in a contact-free way. A set of novel signal processing schemes is used to extract submillimeter heartbeat motion amid other interfering movements. We successfully prototype the first real-time heartbeat monitoring system built with a commodity smart speaker. Experimental results show that the proposed system can accurately monitor a target's heartbeat, with a median heart rate estimation error of 0.75 beat per minute (bpm) and a median heartbeat interval estimation error of 13.28 ms (less than 1.8%), outperforming even some popular commodity products on the market.
